title: Rate propagation glitch leading to persistent batcher silence and tail latency surge
creator: Ava Martinez
description: During a high-throughput ramp on hosted, the continuous-batcher experienced prolonged formation silence across a subset of nodes, which led to sustained tail latency increases for chat and completion routes. This ticket contains the investigation summary, immediate mitigations applied, and actionable follow-ups to prevent recurrence.
incident_timeline: 2026-02-28 09:04 UTC — First alerts: p95/p99 for /v1/chat/completions increased on region-us-west-2. Ops page showed drop in batches formed on several batcher pods.
2026-02-28 09:12 UTC — Safe-mode routing enabled for affected customer routes to fall back to smaller-capacity model variants to protect external SLAs.
2026-02-28 09:20 UTC — On-call identified batcher metrics: active_slots=high, formation_rate=near-zero, inflight_queue growing; no obvious CPU/GPU saturation.
2026-02-28 09:32 UTC — Deployed a rolling restart of the slot-coordinator process on affected shards; immediate partial recovery observed but not full.

2026-02-28 10:05 UTC — Root-cause hypothesis refined: token-rate propagation from rate-limiter to batcher had a negative feedback loop when upstream token-rate drop occurred, combined with autoscaler fast-shrink policy which removed a small number of warm nodes causing KV-cache churn.

2026-02-28 11:00 UTC — Temporary mitigations: increased batcher formation heartbeat, disabled aggressive autoscaler shrink in the affected AZ, added short-term sticky routing to nodes with warm KV state.
2026-02-28 13:00 UTC — p99 returned close to baseline; monitoring continued throughout the day for regressions. Incident declared for follow-up actions.
impact_summary: Approximately 12% of production RPCs to chat/completions in us-west-2 experienced >2x tail latency for ~3 hours; a small set of high-throughput customers observed degraded throughput and higher cost due to fallbacks. No user data loss or incorrect outputs were detected.
root_cause_analysis: Primary: token-rate propagation bug in the rate-limiter->batch-coordinator handshake where a transient upstream rate drop set the coordinator into a zero-formation state until a full heartbeat cycle — effectively a latching silence.

Secondary contributing factor: autoscaler shrink policy removed 2 warm nodes during the incident window; eviction of KV cache amplified the time to recover because batchers prefer slot-local KV entries when forming batches.
Tertiary: lack of a hard guardrail for minimum formation rate and insufficient observability on per-slot cold/warm state transitions.
mitigations_applied: Increased batcher heartbeat frequency from 1s -> 250ms for affected shards (temporary) to reduce latch duration.
Disabled autoscaler aggressive shrink for region-us-west-2 for 24h and adjusted shrink threshold for subsequent deployments.
Added sticky routing to prefer nodes with warm KV caches for high-throughput routes while the cluster healed.
Deployed a quick patch that ensures coordinator does not accept a zero-formation-window as final state until two consecutive heartbeat cycles (rollback-safe).
action_items: ENG-25799-A1: Ship a deterministic fix to the rate propagation handshake to guarantee monotonic decay (owner: Daniel Kim, estimate: 3d, due: 2026-03-12) — add unit tests and integration test in batcher-sim.

ENG-25799-A2: Implement a minimum formation-rate guardrail (configurable) in the coordinator so formation_rate < X triggers backoff control instead of latch (owner: Priya Shah, estimate: 2d, due: 2026-03-16).
ENG-25799-A3: Change autoscaler shrink policy to require sustained underutilization for 5m before node removal (owner: Infra SRE team, estimate: 2d, due: 2026-03-15).
ENG-25799-A4: Add a KV-cache warmness metric and per-slot heatmap to Console dashboards; create alert when fraction of cold slots > 30% (owner: Observability team, estimate: 4d, due: 2026-03-20).
ENG-25799-A5: Add a regression test to CI that simulates upstream rate cliffs + autoscaler shrink to validate no latching behavior (owner: Test Reliability, estimate: 3d, due: 2026-03-18).

ENG-25799-A6: Run a targeted canary (runtime-1.19) with the new handshake and autoscaler tuning in staging for 48h before global rollout (owner: Release Manager, estimate: 1d coordination, due: 2026-03-22).
owners_and_followups: Daniel Kim — implement handshake fix, land PR, and shepherd to canary.
Priya Shah — coordinator config and guardrail rollout; follow up on impact to throughput (A/B test).
Infra SRE — autoscaler policy change and retroactive audit of recent shrink events correlated with latency spikes.
Observability — new dashboards and alerting; link to dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/kv-warmness-us-west-2
Test Reliability — add deterministic simulator scenario to batcher-sim and nightly CI.
Release Manager — run targeted canary and confirm metrics: p95/p99, batch formation rate, KV-local hit-rate.
postmortem_notes: We observed a classic negative feedback latch — small transient upstream changes should not be able to put the coordinator into a zero-formation terminal state.
KV-cache warmness significantly reduces re-formation cost; autoscaler decisions should consider cache heat as a soft affinity signal for eviction avoidance.
Operational playbooks need a dedicated runbook for batcher-silence that includes quick disable of aggressive shrink and sticky routing steps.
